newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Terranova buys Brazil timberlands.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Terranova buys Brazil timberlands.

text.p: Chilean forestry group Terranova SA announced a major timber investment in southern Brazil, where it will buy 13,500 hectares of evergreen woods from Grupo Gerdau Emprendimentos Ltda of Brazil's Gerdau, Terranova said.
Terranova will pay $40 million for the pine lands plus a sawmill under the deal signed on April 18, Terranova said in the statement filed with the Chilean Stocks and Securities Superintendent.
The letter was not more specific about where the land is located and no further details on the deal were available.

Terranova reported $16.4 million profits in 1996 on an operating loss of $708,000 and an operating gain of $17.1 million. Like much of the Chilean forestry industry, Terranova's profits have lagged since early 1996 on soft paper pulp prices.
